findings.finding_label: Primary econometric models (2020–2021 panel): Effect of regulation and regulatory enforcement (REGU) on social tariff implementation (DIST)
findings.outcome_and_polarity: DIST (Degree of Implementation of the Social Tariff Index, in percentage points 0–100%): ratio of residential customers registered in the ~50%-discounted social tariff in Copasa-MG/Copanor billing databases to low-income network-connected CadÚnico households eligible for the social tariff, capped at 100%. Higher values mean BETTER household water/sanitation affordability/subsidy coverage among network-connected poor households.

findings.exact_estimate: Statewide mean DIST increased from 68.28% (SD = 24.76%, min = 12.51%, max = 100%) in 2020 (before inspection) to 87.53% (SD = 15.13%, min = 24.22%, max = 100%) in 2021 (after inspection) across N = 572 municipalities (Table 3). Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (two-sided asymptotic): 419 positive ranks (73.3%), 48 negative ranks (8.4%), 105 draws (18.4%), Z = -17.557, p = 0.000 (Table 4). All 12 macro-regions also showed statistically significant increases (one-sided exact Wilcoxon p <= 0.004). Municipal count with DIST < 50% fell from 151 (of 581) in 2020 to 17 (of 583) in 2021 (PDF pp. 7–9).

Higher DIST generally reflects higher relative social-tariff enrollment among registered eligible households, EXCEPT for CUUR, which directly expands the denominator (H_CadUnico) before utility billing records adjust, creating a mechanical/lag inverse relationship with the ratio even while absolute beneficiary counts may increase (PDF pp. 16–17, 20).

headline_result_summary: Across 572 municipalities served by Copasa-MG in Minas Gerais, Brazil, state regulatory enforcement and new social-tariff regulation by Arsae-MG (an August 2020 surprise economic inspection, State Law No. 23,670/2020, and Regulation Arsae-MG No. 150/2021 establishing annual inspections, publicity standards, and online enrollment, although capping the discounted bracket at <=20 m3/month) was associated with a statistically significant increase in the Degree of Implementation of the Social Tariff (DIST Index). Unadjusted mean DIST rose from 68.28% in 2020 to 87.53% in 2021 (Wilcoxon Z = -17.557, p < 0.001), and adjusted random-effects GLS panel regressions estimated an increase of 18.82 to 19.21 percentage points in 2020–2021 (p < 0.01) and 13.13 to 13.48 percentage points in an extended 2018–2021 robustness panel (p < 0.01). By contrast, local participatory sanitation governance via a Municipal Sanitation Fund/Council/Plan (MSF) had a statistically null effect on social-tariff implementation (0.23 to 0.33 percentage points, p > 0.10).
specification_or_coding_pitfalls: 1. No untreated counterfactual (pre-post indicator only): REGU is simply a post-intervention year dummy (REGU = 1 in 2021 vs. 0 in 2020 or 2018–2020) applied across all Copasa-MG municipalities; the authors explicitly note that difference-in-differences could not be estimated because no comparable untreated utility/regulator data exist, and DIST had temporarily dipped from 76.1% (2018) and 78.3% (2019) to 68.3% (2020) before rising to 87.53% (2021). 2. Dependent variable rescaling between Table 5 and Table 6: Table 5 models DIST in percentage points (0–100, so REGU = 19.2078 means +19.21 pp and CUUR = -0.3627), whereas Table 6 rescales DIST to a 0–1 proportion (so REGU = 0.1345 means +13.45 pp and CUUR = -0.0037 equals -0.37 pp, though the authors mistakenly describe -0.0037 on p. 17 as 'substantially smaller' and 'close to zero' relative to Table 5). 3. Wilcoxon Z-statistic sign: Table 4 reports negative Z-statistics (e.g., Z = -17.557) by standard Wilcoxon convention even though 419 municipalities increased vs. 48 decreased; a careless coder must not misread the negative Z-statistic as a decrease in DIST. 4. Outcome scope and denominator mechanics: DIST measures subsidy enrollment among low-income CadÚnico households who ALREADY have access to the public water supply network (not new physical connections), is right-censored at 100%, does not verify household-by-household ID matching against inclusion errors, and has a mechanical denominator relationship with CUUR (faster municipal CadÚnico updating expands H_CadUnico in the denominator before utility billing updates, producing a negative coefficient on the ratio even if more poor households receive the tariff). 5. Secondary governance null: If coding participatory municipal governance (Municipal Sanitation Fund/Council/Plan, MSF) rather than state regulatory enforcement (REGU), the effect on DIST is completely null. 6. Benefit cap trade-off: Regulation No. 150/2021 restricted the social tariff discount to consumption <=20 m3/month (Figure 2), which the empirical DIST outcome does not evaluate in terms of actual household bills.
study_design: Pre-post balanced longitudinal municipal panel study (2020–2021 primary panel; 2018–2021 robustness panel) without an untreated control group, using paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and random-effects GLS panel regressions with White period robust standard errors
unit_and_sample_size: Municipalities in Minas Gerais state served by Copasa-MG (and Copanor): primary balanced panel N = 572 municipalities over 2 years, 2020–2021 (1,144 municipality-year observations, covering >600,000 social-tariff households; 9 municipalities with additional providers excluded from 581); robustness balanced panel N = 570 municipalities over 4 years, 2018–2021 (2,280 municipality-year observations)
